name: National Bank of Oman
founded: 1973 (first incorporated bank in Oman; joint stock company; shares listed on MSX)
ownership_summary: At 30 Jun 2026 the Commercial Bank (P.S.Q.C.) of Qatar held 34.90% and Suhail Salim Abdullah Al Mukhaini Bahwan 14.75%; all other holders each held below 10% (50.35% in total). The December 2025 IR page shows 34.90% and 14.74%. The June 2026 presentation says the two holders together hold 49.6% and that government-related holders own more than 30%. The undated FSA register lists the Social Protection Fund at 9.9% and Al Anwar Investments SAOG at 7.55%.

shareholders.holder: Suhail Salim Abdullah Al Mukhaini Bahwan

government_link: Indirect. The June 2026 investor presentation says government institutions hold more than 30% of NBO (S3), and the board includes nominees from the Social Protection Fund, the Public Authority for Social Insurance, the Military and Security Services Pension Fund and the Royal Oman Police (S7). The FSA register (undated) shows the Social Protection Fund at 9.9% (S11). The largest holder is a Qatari bank, not a state entity.
group_structure: Single bank with an Islamic window, Muzn Islamic Banking, and branches in the UAE (Dubai and Abu Dhabi). The Egypt branch is being closed (S1 note 1, S3). One immaterial wholly owned SPV, NBO Global Markets Cayman Limited, is consolidated. The Wholesale Banking segment includes investment banking (asset management, corporate advisory and brokerage for retail and institutional clients) (S1 note 28). The Commercial Bank's Chairman (Deputy Chairman of NBO) and its Group CEO both sit on NBO's board (S7).
footprint: At 30 Jun 2026: 68 branches and 237 ATM and CCDM units in Oman, plus two branches in the UAE (Dubai and Abu Dhabi); the Egypt branch is in legal closure. Market share about 13.6% of loans and 13.5% of deposits at 31 Mar 2026 (S3).
customer_segments: Retail mass, Mazaya (Privilege) preferred banking, Sadara Priority Banking, Private Banking (HNW), Muzn Islamic retail, SME, corporate, government and GREs, financial institutions.
business_lines: Five segments in the H1 2026 statements: Retail Banking (including HNW customers), Wholesale Banking (including investment banking, asset management, corporate advisory and brokerage), International (UAE, Egypt), Islamic Banking (Muzn) and the Funding Center (S1 note 28). Retail revenue and wealth products sit with the Chief Retail & Digital Banking Officer; Private Banking & Segments is led by an AGM (S6). Strategy for 2026-2028 is called PRIME (S3).

capabilities.wealth_summary: NBO runs a three-tier affluent proposition: Mazaya (Privilege) from a 15,000 balance or 1,000 salary transfer, with a certified wealth advisor; Sadara Priority Banking with a dedicated RM and 'Sadara Wealth Management'; and Private Banking, launched on 29 Jun 2022 under Ali Al Lawati and named Best Private Bank in Oman by Euromoney in March 2025. The shelf is global investment funds, structured products (the bank says it was the first in Oman with capital-guaranteed products), securities brokerage, SIPs from OMR 100 a month, lending against securities, and trust and wealth planning through partner networks. NBO is FSA-licensed for Brokerage, Custodian, Investment Manager, Portfolio Management and Fund Administration. In-house funds are the NBO GCC Fund, Global Equity Fund and Money Market Fund (launched 2025); funds under management were OMR 196.6m at 31 Dec 2025. A wealth portal inside the mobile app has offered fund buy/sell and SIPs for Sadara and Mazaya customers since July 2021, and in 2026 customers could subscribe to the OMIFCO IPO through the NBO and Muzn apps. The 2026-2028 PRIME strategy lists API-led partnerships and fintech collaborations.

segments.name: Mazaya (Privilege) Banking
segments.eligibility: Maintain a balance of 15,000 or a salary transfer of 1,000 and above; currency is an image on the page (OMR likely). Dedicated RM and a certified wealth advisor.

segments.name: Sadara Priority Banking
segments.eligibility: Not published on the page opened. Benefits include a dedicated RM, Sadara Elite savings account, Sadara Wealth Management and SIP.

segments.name: Private Banking
segments.eligibility: No threshold on the page; a Key Fact Statement PDF is linked. Infinite credit card, lounge and global investment advisory.

private_banking.detail: Launched 29 Jun 2022 for HNW customers; led by Ali Mustafa Al Lawati (Head of Private Banking since Mar 2021). Services: global investment advisory, global funds, structured products, SIP, trade execution in bonds, equities and FX, lending against marketable securities and real estate, wealth planning and trust services through partner networks. Euromoney named NBO Best Private Bank in Oman (Mar 2025), reporting AUM up 259% over its review period and some UHNW clients moving assets from Swiss banks.

asset_management.detail: In-house, inside Wholesale Banking's investment banking unit (not a separate legal entity). Three open-ended funds: NBO GCC Fund (flagship, CMA-regulated), NBO Global Equity Fund and NBO Money Market Fund (third open-ended fund, public offering closed Feb 2025; daily liquidity, no entry or exit charges per Oct 2025 fact sheet seen in search results). Funds under management OMR 196,629k at 31 Dec 2025 (+45%). FSA activities include Investment Manager, Portfolio Management and Fund Administration. A press item (search results only) names Abdullah Al Jabri as Head of Asset Management; not on the live page.

brokerage.detail: FSA register lists Brokerage (contact Brokerage@nbo.co.om), Custodian and Issue Management (S11). The annual report's segment note says investment banking offers brokerage to retail and institutional clients (S1). Private Banking offers trade execution in bonds, equities and FX (S8). MSX membership and markets covered were not confirmed.

digital_investing.detail: Wealth portal inside the NBO mobile app launched July 2021 for Sadara and Mazaya customers: view portfolio, buy and sell mutual funds, single-fund SIPs, review risk profile, open an investment account (vendor not named). Digital SIP applications added in 2025; OMIFCO IPO subscription through the NBO app and Muzn app in H1 2026. Current feature set of the portal beyond these items was not confirmed.

advisory.detail: Mazaya includes a certified wealth advisor; Sadara and Private Banking provide RM-led investment advisory and financial planning. FSA activity Investment Advice & Research.

discretionary.detail: The FSA register lists Portfolio Management (S11) and Euromoney credits 'portfolio management solutions' (S12), but no NBO page describes a discretionary mandate or minimum.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No model portfolios or robo-advice found. The SIP is described as a portfolio into global and local markets and the app supports single-fund SIPs.

funds_platform.detail: Private Banking offers 'global investment funds' (S8); the wealth portal lets clients buy and sell mutual funds (S13). The third-party fund shelf, platform and fund houses are not named.

structured_products.detail: Private Banking lists structured products; Euromoney 2025 says NBO was the first bank in Oman to introduce structured investment and capital-guaranteed products, quoting returns of up to 24% (S12). Issuers not named.

private_markets.detail: No private equity, private credit or alternatives funds found; real estate appears only as a financing and advice item.

islamic_wealth.detail: Muzn Islamic Banking offers Shari'ah-compliant products and, in 2026, a Shari'ah-compliant IPO subscription through the Muzn app, and runs a Priority Banking proposition. No Shariah-compliant fund or wealth shelf was found.

partners.kind: Core banking and digital technology (vendor-published claim)
partners.what: Vendor customer story describes a 15+ year relationship supporting NBO's core and digital banking; products and date not confirmed (page returned 403; seen in search results only)
2012 alliance to build tailor-made investment product portfolios for NBO private banking customers; no later evidence found
Hackathon (300+ applications) and second cohort of six startups with early access to NBO's Developer Platform and Sandbox; programme concludes in 2026

initiatives.what: Launched a wealth management portal in the mobile app (portfolio view, fund buy/sell, SIP, risk profile) for Sadara and Mazaya customers
Launched the Private Banking proposition for HNW customers
Named Best Private Bank in Oman in the Euromoney Private Banking Awards 2025
Public offering of the NBO Money Market Fund closed, the bank's third open-ended mutual fund
Digital SIP applications through the app, API Gateway for corporates, government and fintech partners, and a second Fintech Accelerator cohort with Developer Platform and Sandbox
Issued a USD 450m Additional Tier 1 instrument (largest ever by an Omani bank, per the annual report); the OMR 115.5m AT1 from April 2021 was redeemed at its first call in April 2026
H1 2026: digital OMIFCO IPO subscription via the NBO and Muzn apps; MoUs with Oman Airports and Ooredoo; partnerships with Sharakah and SMEDA
H1 2026 results authorised: net profit OMR 39.1m (+14.9%); fee income +20.0%; PRIME 2026-2028 strategy in execution

opportunities: PRIME 2026-2028 lists 'Ecosystem & Tech Enablement' to strengthen the ecosystem through 'API-led partnerships & fintech collaborations', and NBO runs an API Gateway, a Developer Platform and Sandbox and a Fintech Accelerator (S3 slide 9, S2 p.18).
The in-app wealth portal dates from July 2021 and covers mutual funds and single-fund SIPs for Sadara and Mazaya customers only; no model portfolios or robo-advice were found (S13).

Mass-affluent and mass entry points are low-ticket (SIP from OMR 100 a month; Mazaya from a 15,000 balance), across about 760,000 retail customers, with fee income up 20% in H1 2026 (S9, S10, S3, S1).
Private Banking's third-party shelf (global funds, structured products, partner-network trust services) is unnamed, so product partners are not fixed in public sources (S8).
Muzn is growing deposits (+12.7%) and already offers Shari'ah-compliant IPO subscription in-app, but no Shariah wealth shelf was found (S1).
barriers: Three in-house funds, FSA licences for brokerage, custody, portfolio management and fund administration, and a named private banking head show a vertically integrated model (S11, S2, S6).
Core banking is reportedly Finastra-based, per a vendor-published story (S17), so integrations would sit on that stack.
Best Private Bank in Oman (Euromoney 2025) and AUM growth suggest the current private banking set-up is viewed as working (S12).
Four senior officers (CIO, COO, Head of Strategy & Transformation, Head of Project Finance & Syndication) left or retired in 2025-2026, and a digital head is not confirmed on the live page (S2).
incumbent_vendors: Finastra: core and digital banking, per vendor-published story, undated (S17)
Reliance Wealth Management: 2012 private banking product alliance, no later evidence (S14)

discrepancies.detail: The June 2026 presentation says government institutions hold more than 30% of NBO, while the FSA register (undated) lists only the Social Protection Fund at 9.9% and Al Anwar Investments at 7.55% above 5%, and the IR pages show no holder other than The Commercial Bank and Suhail Bahwan above 10%.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded shareholders from S3 and S5; government share stated as the bank's claim. The composition of the >30% is not disclosed.

discrepancies.detail: The annual report says NBO more than doubled its 'active' retail customer base over five years, while the June 2026 presentation gives 'approximately 760,000 retail customers' without saying active or registered.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded 760 thousand as retail customers, approximate, basis unspecified.

discrepancies.detail: The AR 2025 management list (published Mar 2026) includes him with no departure footnote, while footnoting three officers who left and one who retired; he was quoted in the role in Apr 2025. The live Senior Management page (checked 2026-10-12) omits him although it lists six other AGM/DGM officers.
discrepancies.resolution: role_status set to 'Conflicting sources'. Unresolved: no appointment or departure news found in role-based searches; re-check NBO's page and the FY2026 report.

discrepancies.detail: The official biography gives a B.Sc. in Business Administration from Boston University; the Jul 2020 appointment release calls it a BSc in Management, Finance and Accounting from Boston University.

open_items: Merger check 2024-2026: no merger, takeover or acquisition involving NBO was found in the H1 2026 statements, the annual report, the IR pages or search results. A 2018-19 NBO and Bank Dhofar merger discussion is mentioned in search results but was abandoned in 2019 and is outside the review window.
MSX ticker NBOB is taken from a data-provider URL (Simply Wall St) seen in search results; it is not given on the NBO pages opened. Confirm on msx.om.
No wealth or private banking client asset figure, no investing user numbers and no AUM beyond the OMR 196.6m fiduciary figure are published.
The wealth portal feature set is described only by a July 2021 article; no newer description was found. The app store listing was not opened.

A press item (Al Bawaba, search results only, page returned 403) announces Abdullah Al Jabri as Head of Asset Management; the date and current status were not verified and he is not on the live management page.
Eligibility for Sadara and Private Banking was not published on the pages opened; a Key Fact Statement PDF for Private Banking is linked but was not read.
Finastra relationship is from a vendor-published, undated story (page returned 403); module scope and whether it is still current are unconfirmed.
Q3 2026 results were not published on the IR page on 12 Oct 2026. Re-check late October.
